verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              स कर्णं कर्णीना कर्णे पुनर्विव्याध फाल्गुनिः। शरैः पञ्चाशता चैनमविध्यत् कोपयन् भृशम्॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Once more did the son of Arjuna pierced Karna on his car, with barbed arrows and then for angering the latter, again pierced him with fifty shafts more.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिविव्याध राधेयस्तावद्भिरथ तं पुनः।  शरैराचितसर्वाङ्गो बहुशोभत भारत॥२॥
कर्णं चाप्यकरोत्क्रुद्धो रुधिरोत्पीडवाहिनम्।  कर्णोऽपि विबभौ शूरः शरैश्छिन्नोऽसृगाप्लुतः॥३॥
तावुभौ शरचित्राङ्गौ रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ।  बभूवतुर्महात्मानौ पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥४॥
verses.english: Then both those high-souled warriors, mangled with arrow-wounds and steeped in blood, appeared like two Kinshukas covered with blossom,

verses.sanskrit: अथ कर्णस्य सचिवान् षट् शूरांश्चित्रयोधिनः।  साश्वसूतध्वजरथान् सौभद्रो निजघान ह॥५॥
verses.english: Then Subhadra's son slew six of Karna's ministers all versed in various modes of warfare, together with their horses, charioteer, car and standards.

verses.sanskrit: तथेतरान् महेष्वासान् दशभिर्दशभिः शरैः।  प्रत्यविध्यदसंभ्रान्तस्तद‌द्भुतमिवाभवत्॥६॥
verses.english: Then Abhimanyu fearlessly pierced the rest of the mighty car-warriors in return, with ten shafts each; that feat of his seemed exceedingly wonderful.

verses.sanskrit: मागधस्य तथा पुत्रं हत्वा षड्भिरजिह्मगैः।  साश्वं ससूतं तरुणमश्वकेतुमपातयत्॥७॥
verses.english: Thereafter having slain the son of the ruler of the Magadhas with six swift-coursing arrows, Abhimanyu felled the youthful Ashvaketu together with his horses and charioteer.

verses.sanskrit: मार्तिकावतकं भोजं ततः कुञ्जरकेतनम्।  क्षुरप्रेण समुन्मथ्य ननाद विसृजन् शरान्॥८॥
तस्य दौःशासनिर्विद्ध्वा चतुर्भिश्चतुरो हयान्।  सूतमेकेन विध्याध दशभिश्चार्जुनात्मजम्॥९॥
verses.english: Thereupon the son of Drona pierced his four horses with four arrows and charioteer with one shaft and then he pierced Arjuna's son with ten arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दौःशासनिं कार्ष्णिर्विध्वा सप्तभिराशुगैः।  संरम्भाद्रक्तनयनो वाक्यमुच्चैरथाब्रवीत्॥१०॥
verses.english: Thereafter Krishna's nephew having pierced Dushasana's son with ten swiftcoursing arrows, spoke these words at the top of his voice, with eyes red in rage.

verses.sanskrit: पिता तवाहवं त्यक्त्वा गतः कापुरुषो यथा।  दिष्ट्या त्वमपि जानीषे योद्धुं न त्वद्य मोक्ष्यसे॥११॥
verses.english: "Your father has fled from the battle like a veritable coward. It is fortunate that you know how to fight. But today you shall not escape me alive."

verses.sanskrit: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं कर्मारपरिमार्जितम्।  नाराचं विससर्जास्मै तं द्रौणिस्त्रिभिराच्छिनत्॥१२॥
verses.english: Having spoken only these words, he hurled at him a Naracha burnished by the forger himself.

verses.sanskrit: तस्या‌र्जुनिर्ध्वजं छित्त्वा शल्यं त्रिभिरताडयत्।  तं शल्यो नवभिर्बाणैर्गार्ध्रपत्रैरताडयत्॥१३॥
हृद्यसंभ्रान्तवद्राजंस्तद‌द्भुतमिवाभवत्।  तस्यार्जुनिर्ध्वजं छित्त्वा हत्वोभौ पार्ष्णिसारथी॥१४॥
तं विव्याधायसैः षड्भिः सोपाक्रामद्रथान्तरम्।  शत्रुञ्जयं चन्द्रकेतुं मेघवेगं सुवर्चसम्॥१५॥
सूर्यभासं च पञ्चैतान् हत्वा विव्याध सौबलम्।  तं सौबलस्त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वा दुर्योधनमथाब्रवीत्॥१६॥
verses.english: Then having slain Satrunjaya, Chandraketu, Meghavega, Suvarchasam and Suryabhasa, he pierced the son of Subala. Subala then piercing him with three arrows, thus addressed Duryodhana-

verses.sanskrit: सर्व एनं विमथ्नीमः पुरैकैकं हिनस्ति नः।  अथाब्रवीत् पुनर्द्रोणं कर्णो वैकर्तनो रणे॥१७॥
पुरा सर्वान् प्रमथ्नाति ब्रह्यस्य वधमाशु नः।  ततो द्रोणो महेष्वासः सर्वांस्तान् प्रत्यभाषत॥१८॥
verses.english: "Tell us the means of his death, before he slays us all.” Thereupon the fierce bow-man Drona replied to them all saying-

verses.sanskrit: अस्ति वाऽस्यान्तरं किञ्चित् कुमारस्याथ पश्यत।  अण्वप्यस्यान्तरं ह्यद्य चरतः सर्वतोदिशम्॥१९॥
verses.english: "With all your watchfulness, have you been able to detect any weakness in this youthful prince? He is careering in all directions; yet has any of you been able to find out any laches in the prince?

verses.sanskrit: शीघ्रतां नरसिंहस्य पाण्डवेयस्य पश्यत।  धनुर्मण्डलमेवास्य रथमार्गेषु दृश्यते॥२०॥
संदधानस्य विशिखान् शीघ्रं चैव विमुञ्चतः।  आरुजन्नपि मे प्राणान् मोहयन्नपि सायकैः॥२१॥
प्रहर्षयति मां भूयः सौभद्रः परवीरहा।  अति मां नन्दयत्येष सौभद्रो विचरन् रणे॥२२॥
verses.english: Indeed this slayer of hostile heroes, this son of Subhadra is affording me great delight, though with his shafts he is afflicting my vital limbs and confounding my senses. This son of Subhadra careering through the field of battle, delights me greatly.

verses.sanskrit: अन्तरं यस्य संरब्धा न पश्यन्ति महारथाः।  अस्यतो लघुहस्तस्य दिशः सर्वा महेषुभिः॥२३॥
verses.english: In as much as many mighty car-warriors inflamed with rage cannot detect any the slightest weakness in him. I do not find any very great difference between the wielder of the Gandiva bow and this one of great lightness of hands, filling the points of the compass with his mighty shafts.

verses.sanskrit: न विशेषं प्रपश्यामि रणे गाण्डीवधन्वनः।  अथ कर्णः पुनर्द्रोणमाहार्जुनिशराहतः॥२४॥
स्थातव्यमिति तिष्ठामि पीड्यमानोऽभिमन्युना। तेजस्विनः कुमारस्य शराः परमदारुणाः॥२५॥
verses.english: Then once more Karna, afflicted with the arrows of Arjuna's son said to Drona "Afflicted sore by Abhimanyu, I am staying here, only because as a warrior, I should stay here.

verses.sanskrit: क्षिण्वन्ति हृदयं मेऽद्य घोराः पावकतेजसः।  तमाचार्योऽब्रवीत् कर्णं शनकैः प्रहसन्निव॥२६॥
verses.english: The fierce and exceedingly dreadful darts, corroding like fire, of this very furious prince, are this day sucking my heart's strength in battle.” Then softly and with a smile the preceptor replied to Karna saying-

verses.sanskrit: अभेद्यमस्य कवचं युवा चाशुपराक्रमः।  उपदिष्टा मया चास्य पितुः कवचधारणा॥२७॥
verses.english: "O Karna! This Abhimanyu is faithful, his prowess is great and his armour is incapable of being penetrated into. I have taught the father of this hero, the diverse methods of wearing coats of mail; assuredly this subjugator of hostile fortresses, knows all those methods of wearing armours. But exerting yourself carefully, you can, with arrows cut-off his bow, his bowstring.

verses.sanskrit: तामेष निखिलां वेत्ति ध्रुवं परपुरञ्जयः।  शक्यं त्वस्य धनुश्छेत्तुं ज्यां च बाणैः समाहितैः॥२८॥
अभीषूंश्च हयांश्चैव तथोभौ पार्ष्णिसारथी।  एतत्कुरु महेष्वास राधेय यदि शक्यते॥२९॥
verses.english: The reins of his steeds and his two supporters of the flanks. O mighty bow-man, 0 son of Radha, if you are competent, then do all these.

verses.sanskrit: अथैनं विमुखीकृत्य पश्चात् प्रहरणं कुरु।  सधनुष्को न शक्योऽयमपि जेतुं सुरासुरैः॥३०॥
verses.english: Then compelling him to turn his face away from the field, do you strike him from behind. As long as he wields the bow, he is incapable of being defeated even by all the Gods and the Asuras united together.

verses.sanskrit: विरथं विधनुष्कं च कुरुष्वैनं यदीच्छसि।  तदाचार्यवचः श्रुत्वा कर्णो वैकर्तनस्त्वरन्॥३१॥
verses.english: So if you can, deprive him of the use of his car and his bow.” Then, Vikartana's son, Karna, hearing those words of the preceptor quickly cut-off Abhimanyu's bow with his arrows, when the latter was light-handedly scattering his shafts. Then Kritavarman of the Bhoja race, slew his steeds and Kripa the son of Gautama dispatched his two flanksupporters.

verses.sanskrit: अस्यतो लघुहस्तस्य पृषत्कैर्धनुराच्छिनत्।  अश्वानस्यावधीद्भोजो गौतमः पार्ष्णिसारथी॥३२॥
शेषास्तु च्छिन्नधन्वानं शरवर्षैरवाकिरन्।  त्वरमाणास्त्वराकाले विरथं षण्महारथाः॥३३॥
verses.english: The rest covered him with arrowy showers, when he was deprived of the use of his bow. Then these six mighty car-warriors with great activity, when activity was so necessary, ruthlessly covered that young careless hero who was fighting with them single-handedly, with showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: शरवर्षैरकरुणा बालमेकमवाकिरन्।  सच्छिन्नधन्वा विरथः स्वधर्ममनुपालयन्॥३४॥
खड्गचर्मधरः श्रीमानुत्पपात विहायसा।  मार्गैः सकौशिकाद्यैश्च लाघवेन बलेन च॥३५॥
verses.english: Then that handsome hero whose car had been rendered useless and whose bow had been cut-off, grasping his sword and buckler and remembering his duty, jumped up into the sky.

verses.sanskrit: आर्जुनिर्व्यचरद्व्योम्नि भृशं वै पक्षिराडिव। मय्येव निपतत्येष सासिरित्यूर्ध्वदृष्टयः॥३६॥
verses.english: Exhibiting great prowess and great lightness, Arjuna's son roved in the air like the king of the birds, in various motions, known as Kaushika and others.

verses.sanskrit: विव्यधुस्तं महेष्वासं समरे छिद्रदर्शिनः।  तस्य द्रोणोऽच्छिनन्मुष्टौ खड्गं मणिमयत्सरुम्॥३७॥
verses.english: “With the sword in his hand he may fall upon me,'-thinking thus those mighty bowmen with their eyes up-turned and very watchful for finding Abhimanyu's weakness, began to pierce him.

verses.sanskrit: क्षुरप्रेण महातेजास्त्वरमाणः सपत्नजित्।  राधेयो निशितैर्बाणैर्व्यधमच्चर्म चोत्तमम्॥३८॥
व्यसिचर्मेषुपूर्णाङ्गः सोऽन्तरिक्षात् पुनः क्षितिम्। आस्थितश्चक्रमुद्यम्य द्रोणं क्रुद्धोऽभ्यधावत॥३९॥
verses.english: Then Radha's son also cut-off his excellent buckler with many sharp arrows. Then deprived of his sword and his shield he came down from the sky upon the ground, with all his limbs intact. Then raising a car-wheel, he furiously rushed against Drona.

verses.sanskrit: स चक्ररेणूज्ज्वलशोभिताङ्गोबभावतीवोज्ज्वलचक्रपाणिः।  रणेऽभिमन्युः क्षणमास रौद्रः स वासुदेवानुकृतिं प्रकुर्वन्॥४०॥
verses.english: His person shining with the dust from the car-wheel and himself wielding the car-wheel in his upraised arm, Abhimanyu appeared highly beautiful and for a while imitating the son of Vasudeva, he became terrible fierce in that battle.

verses.sanskrit: स्रुतरुधिरकृतैकरागवस्त्रो भ्रुकुटिपुटाकुलितोऽतिसिंहनादः।  प्रभुरमितबलो रणेऽभिमन्युर्नृपवरमध्यगतो भृशं व्यराजत्॥४१॥
verses.english: With his robes dyed with the blood flowing in profusion (from his wounds), with his brows formidable in consequence of the wrinkles thereon, himself sending up loud war-cries, that highly powerful Abhimanyu appeared superbly beautiful staying in the midst of those foremost of kings.
